aria: Animated recap of the Timberwolves' 115 to 100 home win over Utah: LaMelo Ball's three with 6:45 left in the second quarter, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Ayo Dosunmu's 26 points, the top scorers, how Minnesota won, and the next game against Dallas.
notes: Final score and quarter scores from the Field Level Media game story (via Yardbarker and The Sports Leader): Minnesota led 28–25 after one, 57–51 at the half and 90–78 after three, and won the fourth 25–22. The halftime and end-of-third scores also match Yahoo Sports' Jazz recap. The AP story (via ABC News and KFGO) gives 90–72 after three, which does not add up to the 115–100 final with the fourth-quarter score, so the 90–78 figure is used. Minnesota's biggest lead, 19, is from the AP. The sports data feed wasn't available for this recap; records are from the site's standings after Sunday's games (Minnesota 8–3, Dallas 6–4).

Points: Dosunmu 26 (7 of 13, 4 of 5 from three, 8 of 8 free throws per the AP and RotoWire via CBS Sports), Ball 24 (10 of 20) and Gobert 10 with 15 rebounds (AP and Field Level Media), McDaniels 16 on 5 of 9 with 6 rebounds and Hyland 14 (AP and SB Nation's Canis Hoopus via Yahoo Sports), Lyles 9, Shannon Jr. 5 and Kuminga 4 (Canis Hoopus), Beringer 4 (Field Level Media) and Clark 3 (Canis Hoopus' bench recap via Yahoo Sports). No full box score could be read, so the player points were filled in from these written recaps; they add up to the team's 115. Team shooting (38 of 77, 12 of 32 from three; Utah 37 of 87, 7 of 24) is from Field Level Media and Minnesota's 27 of 32 free throws from the AP. Utah's 19 made free throws follow from its 100 points, 37 field goals and 7 threes. Utah's own biggest lead isn't confirmed by a written source, so only Minnesota's is shown.

The play of the game is an original illustration of LaMelo Ball's three-pointer with 6:45 left in the second quarter that made it 43–33 (Field Level Media). Canis Hoopus notes Minnesota led by as many as 10 in the first half. The recaps don't describe the move, so it is drawn as the template's plain pull-up. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

Next: Minnesota hosts Dallas on Thursday at 8:00 PM ET (Plain Text Sports schedule; Canis Hoopus lists 7:00 PM Central), the first game of an eight-game homestand (AP). Minnesota is 5–2 without Anthony Edwards, per the AP.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Minnesota Timberwolves or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Ball’s listed 6-foot-7 and 180 pounds (Basketball-Reference), wearing No. 1 (Wikipedia). The only reported wingspan, from NBADraft.net's pre-draft workouts, equals his 6-foot-6 measured height, so his arms are drawn at a 1.0 ratio. It is an original silhouette with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
